title: Rework GPU fleet controller to event-driven state machine and decouple capacity-planner APIs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: We have accumulated multiple overlapping reconciliation loops, ad-hoc state transitions, and cloud SDK usage patterns across the GPU fleet controller and the capacity planner. This ticket standardizes node lifecycle semantics by replacing periodic-heavy reconciliation with an event-driven state machine, decoupling capacity planning APIs from per-node orchestration, and upgrading the cloud provider SDKs to address latent race conditions and reduce CPU pressure. The goal is to make node transitions deterministic, reduce autoscaler jitter, and lower controller resource usage without changing external autoscaler behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical node-state machine implementation used by controller and capacity-planner components
No more periodic full-cluster reconciles for normal steady-state operations (reconciles only on events or missed-heartbeat backoff)
Cloud SDKs upgraded and wrapped with idempotent helpers; documented breaking changes and fallbacks
End-to-end tests that validate drain -> deallocate -> terminate -> cleanup with k8s finalizers
Perf regression: control-plane CPU for controller pods reduced by >= 40% under representative load
Failure modes tested: API timeouts, transient provider 5xx, re-queued events; system recovers without duplicate allocations
proposed_solution: Introduce an explicit event-driven state machine (states: Unknown -> Ready -> Draining -> Terminating -> Deleting -> Deleted) and centralize transition logic in a new controller package. Replace ad-hoc periodic reconciles with watch-driven handlers + bounded retry/backoff. Decouple capacity-planner by providing a stable 'allocation intent' API that returns a reservation token instead of mutating node records directly. Wrap cloud provider calls (create/detach/terminate) in idempotent helpers with retries and circuit-breaker semantics. Add k8s finalizer usage for graceful cleanup and update e2e suites to simulate provider flakiness. Add feature flag to toggle event-driven mode for canary rollouts.
rollout_plan: 2) Unit + integration tests on CI (new state-machine tests and cloud-wrapper mocks)
3) Staging canary: enable for 10% of autoscaler traffic and observe metrics for 48h
4) Shadow mode in production: event-driven controller runs alongside old controller but does not mutate real allocations for 24h
5) Gradual enablement: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with rollback windows
6) Post-rollout: remove old code paths and cleanup feature flag in a follow-up maintenance PR
comments: 2025-12-11 - Aisha Khan: Initial spike found three distinct reconcile loops touching Node objects. Created high-level plan to centralize transitions.

2026-01-28 - Design review (Pranav Shah): OK with state names and finalizer approach; requested clearer observability around transition latencies.
2026-02-10 - Security (Lena Ortiz): Reviewed cloud-sdk upgrade plan; no secrets handling changes; recommend staged KMS key rotation testing.
2026-02-25 - Marco Silva: Found a race when two allocation intents are created for the same node. Added token compare-and-swap to allocation API to ensure single-writer semantics.
2026-03-08 - Perf benchmark: simulated 5% cluster churn; avg controller CPU reduced by 48% and median node_provision_latency improved by 120ms.
2026-03-11 - QA: Added e2e case for provider 503 during terminate; controller now retries and honors finalizer until confirmed deleted. QA recommends increasing graceful timeout for on-prem nodes.
